synthesis.headline: Only 4 of 100 would buy; 49% of price-sensitive skeptics (income <$75k, skepticism ≥50) reject $29 as an unaffordable weekly fee with unproven savings.

findings.claim: 87% of price-sensitive skeptics (income <$75k, skepticism ≥50) cannot tell whether $29 is weekly, monthly, or one-time, and treat it as a weekly cost they cannot afford.
91% of high-skepticism users (skepticism ≥60) demand a money-back guarantee or third-party validation before trusting the '$40/week savings' claim.
86% of low-tech-comfort users (tech_comfort ≤50) fear hidden auto-renewal and won't start without a no-card free trial or explicit cancellation policy.

highest_leverage_edit.proposed_text: $29/month — 30-day money-back guarantee if you don't save $40/week
highest_leverage_edit.rationale: Reframes the ambiguous $29 as a monthly fee (not weekly) and adds the guarantee that 91% of high-skepticism users demand, directly addressing the top two conversion blockers.

synthesis.who_you_are_losing: Price-sensitive families earning <$75k who think $29 is a weekly fee and see no proof it saves $40/week.
synthesis.who_you_are_winning: Mid-income (40-150k), tech-comfortable (tech_comfort ≥60) professionals who value time savings over price and trust the product vision.
